Drug resistance
rows.explainer:
We apply a larger adjustment accounting for the potential development of drug resistance in DRC, Mozambique, and Uganda than in other countries because we believe current levels of resistance to SP are higher in East Africa, and we assume that the risk of SMC campaigns accelerating drug resistance is higher in areas with higher baseline resistance.

“SP has been used alone for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) for roughly 20 years. This is likely to have contributed to resistance to SP developing in Tanzania and East Africa, and SP is no longer very effective in those places for IPTp. However, it is still effective in much of the rest of Africa. A mutation associated with a particularly high level of SP resistance that appeared in Southeast Asia (the DHFR 164 mutation) also appeared in Uganda but has not spread in Africa.” GiveWell's non-verbatim summary of a conversa

Scenario 2: Global Fund and/or PMI would replace the grantee's costs
rows.explainer:
We think it is unlikely that these funders would support the work this grant will support. SMC is a new program in Mozambique, and its effectiveness has not yet been demonstrated in an RCT. The PNCM told us that it does not expect other funders to contribute to SMC at this time, though it expects that they will do so in the future.

2023 update: An RCT of SMC has now occurred in Mozambique, but we have not yet updated our funging assumptions accordingly. We plan to investigate this in the near future.
